en: Although often mistakenly thought to be in Davao City, Mount Apo is actually located in the provinces of Davao del Sur and North Cotabato.
Many mistakenly view Taal as a simple crater, but it is actually a complex volcano featuring an island within a lake.
Many think Mount Pulag is the highest, but Mount Apo in Mindanao is actually the tallest peak in the Philippines.
Although geographically isolated, Palawan is administratively part of the Mimaropa region in Luzon, not the Visayas.
Many mistakenly believe the longest river is in Mindanao, but the Cagayan River in Luzon is actually the longest.
Despite its name, the Philippine Sea is on the eastern side, while the West Philippine Sea is on the west.
Although its name includes the word 'bay,' Laguna de Bay is actually a large freshwater lake, not an ocean bay.
Many think the Spanish built the Banaue Rice Terraces, but the Ifugao people actually constructed them over 2,000 years ago.
Although popular with surfers, Siargao Island is in Mindanao's Caraga region, not the Visayas.
Many confuse its location, but the critically endangered tamaraw is endemic to the island of Mindoro, not Mindanao.
Although it has a regional government, the Cordillera Administrative Region is composed of six provinces, not just one.
Many still cite the old number, but the Philippines actually has 7,641 islands, not the commonly believed 7,107.
